title: First Stage of Labor Anatomy: Cervical Dilation & Guide
description: Understand first stage of labor anatomy, including rhythmic uterine contractions, cervical effacement and dilation to ten centimeters, and head engagement.
h1: First Stage of Labor Anatomy: Cervical Effacement and Dilation
blurb: Rhythmic myometrial contractions pull the collagen-rich cervix upward, thinning (effacing) and dilating the cervical canal to a full ten centimeters.
lead: During the first stage of labor, coordinated waves of smooth muscle contraction gradually draw the firm cervical canal upward until it opens to ten centimeters. In this illustrated guide to first stage of labor anatomy, we examine 20 documented structures—including uterine contractions, myometrium, uterine fundus, lower uterine segment—linking regional topography, tissue architecture, physiological mechanisms, and clinical reasoning.
overview: During the first stage of labor, coordinated waves of smooth muscle contraction gradually draw the firm cervical canal upward until it opens to ten centimeters. The first stage of labor begins when contractions produce progressive cervical change and ends at complete cervical dilation, approximately 10 cm. Effacement shortens and thins the cervix as it dilates. Latent and active phases vary; active labor is often defined around 6 cm, not a fixed timetable for every person. The NEW digital cutaway models a fetus before birth and a partially opening cervix. It is not an obstetric examination or an exact centimeter measurement. A second NONPREGNANT regional cervix image is provided separately for structural context. Fetal membranes may remain intact or rupture. Heavy bleeding, severe persistent pain or reduced fetal movement requires clinical assessment. questions.question: When does the first stage of labor begin and end?
questions.answer: It begins when uterine contractions produce progressive cervical change and ends at complete cervical dilation, approximately 10 cm. It does not end with delivery of placenta.

questions.question: What is cervical effacement during labor?
questions.answer: Effacement means thinning and shortening of the cervix. Dilation describes enlargement of the cervical opening; both relate to first-stage change.

questions.question: At what dilation is active labor often considered?
questions.answer: Modern clinical descriptions commonly regard active labor as starting around 6 cm, rather than treating 4 cm as a universal boundary. Care decisions and normal progress require individual assessment.

questions.question: Must the amniotic membranes rupture before contractions begin?
questions.answer: No. Membrane rupture may occur before or during labor, and timing differs. Suspected rupture requires appropriate clinical assessment, not comparison with a still teaching plate.

questions.question: Can the labor-stage-one image measure cervical dilation?
questions.answer: No. The new digital cutaway models a partly opening cervix and a fetus still inside the uterus, but cannot give an individual patient’s dilation in centimeters. A second nonpregnant cervix image is separately identified as structural context only.
